extracted.intended_audience: readers of Jefferson's correspondence; historians, statesmen, naturalists and contemporaneous correspondents
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of Thomas Jefferson's 1787 letters on diplomacy, commerce, natural history, pedagogy, and observations on European affairs, containing multiple prescriptive remarks and practical guidance for collectors, diplomats, merchants, and public servants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of physical diagrams in teaching geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: I have reflected on your idea of wooden or ivory diagrams... I should think wood as good as ivory; and that in this case, it might add to the improvement of the young gentlemen, that they should make the figures themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend furnishing students with a piece of veneer and simple tools (penknife and wooden rule); pasteboards or common cards may be convenient. Note the pedagogical benefit of students constructing figures themselves and practical considerations about reconciling the thickness of physical figures with the notion of a mathematical line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy in prisoner redemption negotiations
rubrics_metrics.description: Till this is done, I shall take no other step than the preparatory one, of destroying at Algiers all idea of our intending to redeem the prisoners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let it transpire, on any account, that the public will interest themselves for their redemption; the religious order advised absolute secrecy, and Jefferson believed even relations of the captives should not be told. Use secrecy strategically to avoid increasing captors' demands or making vessels targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use customary European rates for ransom (not Spanish price)
rubrics_metrics.description: By authorizing me to redeem at the prices usually paid by the European nations, Congress, I suppose, could not mean the Spanish price, which is not only unusual but unprecedented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refuse to pay the unusually high Spanish rate unless further instructed; paying such a price would incentivize pirates and make American vessels prime targets. Follow established European norms for redemption pricing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and funding prerequisite for prisoner redemption
rubrics_metrics.description: The prisoners redeemed by the religious order of Mathurins cost about four hundred dollars each... Supposing that their redemption, clothing, feeding, and transportation should amount to five hundred dollars each, there must be, at least, a sum of ten thousand dollars set apart for this purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not proceed with redemptions until the commissioners of the treasury place the necessary funds under the minister's orders; estimate per-capita cost and set aside an aggregate fund before active measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect exact descriptions of antiquities without theorizing
rubrics_metrics.description: I wish that the persons who go thither, would make very exact descriptions of what they see of that kind, without forming any theories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposit 'naked' factual descriptions in society transactions; avoid premature theorizing because once a theory is formed, imagination will bias observation. Emphasize patient accumulation of facts before interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patience and observation in resolving questions of antiquity
rubrics_metrics.description: Patience and observation may enable us, in time, to solve the problem, whether those who formed the scattering monuments... were colonies sent off from Mexico or the founders of Mexico itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate waiting for more facts; enable gradual, evidence-based resolution of competing hypotheses rather than rushing to conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground geological inference on diverse field observations; avoid premature unified theories
rubrics_metrics.description: This variety proves they have not been formed by subsidence... nor is it probable that convulsions have deformed every spot of the earth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comparative field observation (e.g., strata orientations in different regions) to test earth-formation hypotheses; be skeptical of single-cause theories (subsidence, rotation, universal convulsions) when empirical variety contradicts them. Consider growth-layer models for rock formation where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for sending biological specimens to naturalists
rubrics_metrics.description: I am happy to be able to present to you... the bones and skin of a moose, the horns of another... I give you their popular names, as it rests with yourself to decide their real names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send as complete specimens as possible (skeleton, skin, horns) in condition suitable for stuffing; indicate popular/local names but leave scientific identification to the expert; caution that isolated specimens may not represent ordinary size or variation—procure additional specimens when possible and note age/condition/measurement limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle for good government: separation and subdivision of powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The first principle of a good government, is certainly a distribution of its powers into executive, judiciary, and legislative, and a subdivision of the latter into two or three branches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comparative analysis of constitutions to demonstrate advantages; an article on Confederations should analyze previous confederations' nature, excellencies, and defects to strengthen appreciation of one's own constitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical political lessons from foreign crises (Holland)
rubrics_metrics.description: Never to have an hereditary officer of any sort: never to let a citizen ally himself with kings: never to call in foreign nations to settle domestic differences: never to suppose that any nation will expose itself to war for us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the Holland events as cautionary lessons for domestic institutional design and foreign policy; avoid hereditary offices, private alliances with monarchs, and reliance on foreign intervention to resolve internal conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutral-trade principle: 'free bottom makes free goods' and naval stores non-contraband
rubrics_metrics.description: In our treaties... we have established the simpler rule, that a free bottom makes free goods... Contraband goods, however, are always excepted, so that they may still be seized; but the same powers have established that naval stores are not contraband: and this may be considered now as the law of nations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat this as the emerging law among neutral powers; anticipate insistence by neutral coalition at the outbreak of war. Note England's historical reluctance to accept the principle and its potential diplomatic consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merchant advisory during European hostilities
rubrics_metrics.description: I have written to our agents in the different ports of France, to put our merchants on their guard, against risking their property in French or English bottoms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise merchants to avoid shipping in belligerent or contested national bottoms when war is probable; pragmatic protective advice based on current diplomatic-military developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution in evaluating exploratory reports: beware imaginative bias
rubrics_metrics.description: He is a person of ingenuity and information. Unfortunately, he has too much imagination. However, if he escapes safely, he will give us new, curious, and useful information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing accounts of explorers, value their potential for new information but remain cautious about claims that may be colored by imagination; verify and corroborate observational reports before accepting theoretical conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical diplomatic leverage: use appointments and patronage to advance trade
rubrics_metrics.description: I had pressed on him the patronage of our trade with the French islands; that he appeared well disposed, and assured me he would favor us as much as his instructions, and the laws of the colonies, would permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ diplomatic appointments and personal influence to secure commercial advantages; consider timing (e.g., the minister's residence in the islands) as an opportunity to press for more favorable trade terms, including via treaty if reciprocal equivalents can be found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice for contributing historical/political writing
rubrics_metrics.description: The article of Confederations is certainly worthy of your pen. It would form a most interesting addition, to show, what has been the nature of the Confederations which have existed hitherto, what were their excellencies, and what their defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When composing political prose, include comparative historical analysis highlighting strengths and weaknesses of prior systems to better argue for the merits of the current constitution.
